summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, bilateral below-knee amputations, and a history of multidrug-resistant urinary tract infections presented with nausea, vomiting, and fever. She developed septic shock with hypotension and hyperkalemia, requiring ICU admission. Initial broad-spectrum antibiotics were given, later de-escalated to ciprofloxacin after urine culture identified Klebsiella pneumoniae sensitive to ciprofloxacin. Her acute kidney injury, attributed to pre-renal causes from hypovolemia, improved with intravenous fluids. A central line was placed for antibiotic access and later removed. She was discharged home on oral ciprofloxacin with stable vital signs and improved renal function, with follow-up planned with her primary care provider.
